title: Last-Write-Wins Memory: Isolating Deterministic Overwrite Semantics for Long-Context Conflict Resolution

contributions.purpose: Resolve conflicting fact versions in LLM agent memory at the source rather than relying on the language model during reasoning.
contributions.mechanism: LWW-KO, a memory system applying last-write-wins deterministic overwrite semantics to structured knowledge objects, filtering stale fact versions before retrieval.
contributions.evaluation: On the FactConsolidation benchmark at 262K tokens, achieves 22% multi-hop accuracy (+13pp over append-only structured memory, p=0.0003) and 78% single-hop; exceeds published baselines by +15pp multi-hop and +18pp single-hop.
contributions.domain: LLM agent long-term memory / conflict resolution
contributions.source_quote: LWW-KO, a memory system that applies last-write-wins overwrite semantics to structured knowledge objects, filtering stale fact versions before retrieval.

contributions.purpose: Isolate the causal effect of overwrite semantics from confounding factors in memory-system performance.
contributions.mechanism: A controlled three-condition experiment separating overwrite semantics from structured extraction and retrieval quality on FactConsolidation.
contributions.evaluation: Shows the 13pp multi-hop improvement is attributable to overwrite semantics rather than structured extraction, with no single-hop trade-off.
contributions.source_quote: A controlled three-condition experiment that isolates the effect of overwrite semantics from confounding factors such as structured extraction and retrieval quality.

contributions.purpose: Characterize the error mode that overwrite semantics fixes in append-only memory baselines.
contributions.mechanism: Error analysis categorizing baseline failures into stale-answer errors (outputting outdated facts) and tracing LWW-KO's improvement to their resolution.
contributions.evaluation: 33% of baseline errors are stale-answer errors, and LWW-KO's resolution of these accounts for 73% of its improvement.
contributions.domain: Error analysis of LLM memory systems
contributions.source_quote: An error analysis revealing that 33% of baseline errors are stale-answer errors (outputting outdated facts), and that LWW-KO's resolution of these errors accounts for 73% of its improvement.

self_declared_provenance.quote: This approach is analogous to last-write-wins (LWW) registers in distributed systems, which sacrifice history for consistency.

While these systems implement CRUD-like operations, they do not explicitly evaluate whether overwrite semantics are the causal factor for conflict resolution performance. Our work isolates this specific mechanism through controlled experimentation.
These methods are complementary to our non-parametric approach: parametric editing modifies the model's internal knowledge, while LWW-KO manages external memory without changing model weights.
